# Get your expenses into the Ledger

Forward receipts by email, upload them, or import a month from Google Drive. Each one is read by AI and waits for your check.

Updated 2026-10-18

## Forward receipts by email

The easiest way for receipts that reach your inbox. Your Ledger has a private address. Everything forwarded there becomes an expense, read by AI and waiting for your check.

### Find your address

Open **Settings > Expenses > Email inbox**. The address looks like `expenses+r7k2m9x4qp@open-ledger.dev`. Click **Copy**. The installer sets it up. If the page says the inbox is not set up, run the installer again.

### Set it up in Gmail, once

1. In Gmail, click the gear, then **See all settings**, then the tab **Forwarding and POP/IMAP**.
2. Click **Add a forwarding address**, paste the address and confirm.
3. Gmail sends a confirmation email to that address, with a code or a link. It shows up in the Ledger under **Email inbox**. Type the code in Gmail and click **Verify**, or click **Open the confirmation link**.
4. Leave **Disable forwarding** selected. You forward only receipts, not all your mail.
5. In the Gmail search box, paste the search from the Ledger page, for example `has:attachment (invoice OR receipt)`. The search on the Ledger page also holds the Hebrew words for invoice and receipt. Add your suppliers if you like: `from:(billing@supplier.com)`.
6. Click the search options icon, then **Create filter**. Tick **Forward it to**, pick the address, and click **Create filter**.

From now on, every matching email goes to the Ledger by itself. To send one by hand, forward it to the same address.

### Outlook

**Settings > Mail > Rules > Add new rule.** Condition: **Has attachment**, and words in the subject such as invoice or receipt. Action: **Forward to** the address.

### What happens to each email

- Each PDF, JPG, PNG, WebP or HEIC attachment becomes one expense. Small logo images are skipped.
- An email with no attachment becomes one expense from its text, marked "From email text, check the amount".
- The same file twice is one expense.
- Only email forwarded from your own addresses counts. The list is under **Allowed senders**, and starts with the owner and assistant emails. Anything else is ignored and listed under **Last received**.
- The address passes through MTN's email gateway, which stores nothing.
- Each forwarded file is read with your Gemini or Anthropic key. When a read fails, the expense still arrives, with the reason in its note: "Not read automatically: ...". Fill in the details by hand.

### Your own domain instead

With your own domain on Cloudflare, an address on it goes straight to your Ledger, with no gateway in between.

1. In the Cloudflare dashboard, left menu: **Compute > Email Service > Email Routing**. If your domain is not in the list, click **Onboard Domain**, pick it, and let Cloudflare add its DNS records.
2. Click the domain, open the **Routing rules** tab and click **Create routing rule**. Custom address, for example `receipts`. Action: **Send to a Worker**. Destination: your Ledger's Worker, `mtn-open-ledger`. Save.
3. Use that address in Gmail as above. The Gmail confirmation shows up under **Email inbox** the same way.

Settings shows no address for this route, since you picked it. The allowed senders and **Last received** work the same.

### A new address

If the address leaks or gets spam, click **Make a new address**. The old one stops at once. Update the Gmail filter with the new one.

## Upload

The quickest way.

1. Open **Expenses** and click **Upload expense**.
2. Pick the file: PDF, JPG or PNG. On a phone, take a photo of the paper receipt.
3. With a Gemini or Anthropic key set, the Ledger reads the supplier, date, amounts and VAT, and fills them in. Check them and save.
4. Without a key, type the details yourself.

To add a reading key after the install, see [Add or change a key](https://open-ledger.dev/en/help/keys-later/).

## A month from Google Drive

For receipts you keep in Google Drive. The Ledger reads them, it never writes to Drive.

### How the folder looks

One main folder for expenses. Inside it, one folder per month named `YYYY-MM`, with that month's receipts as PDF or image files.

For example:

- `Expenses`, the main folder
- `Expenses/2026-09`, with `hosting-invoice.pdf` and `software-receipt.png`
- `Expenses/2026-10`, with October's receipts

Files that sit directly in the main folder are not read. Subfolders inside a month folder are not read either.

### Connect it, once

1. Create a Google service account and its JSON key, and turn on the Drive and Sheets APIs. The steps are in the [Drive setup guide](https://github.com/matanlevanon/open-ledger-il/blob/main/docs/drive-expenses-setup.md) on GitHub.
2. Give the Ledger the key as the secret `GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON`, see [Add or change a key](https://open-ledger.dev/en/help/keys-later/).
3. In Drive, share the main folder with the service account's address, the `client_email` in the key, as **Viewer**. The month folders inherit the share.
4. In **Settings > Expenses**, paste the folder id, the part of the folder's address after `/folders/`, and click **Save folder**.
5. The Ledger checks the folder right after saving. Click **Check folder** any time to run it again. It shows the folder's name and the month folders it found, or the one thing to fix: no key, a key that does not work, or a folder Google does not find because it is not shared with the service account.

### Or: a folder shared by link, with an API key

Shorter, with no service account. The catch: anyone who gets the folder's link reads every receipt in it, with names, addresses and amounts.

1. In console.cloud.google.com, pick or create a project. Open **APIs & Services > Library** and turn on **Google Drive API**, and **Google Sheets API** if you keep an index sheet.
2. **APIs & Services > Credentials > Create credentials > API key.** Under **API restrictions**, allow only those two APIs.
3. In Drive, open the main folder's **Share** dialog. Under **General access**, pick **Anyone with the link**, as **Viewer**.
4. Give the Ledger the key as the secret `GOOGLE_API_KEY`, see [Add or change a key](https://open-ledger.dev/en/help/keys-later/).
5. Save the folder id in **Settings > Expenses**. **Check folder** confirms it reads the folder by link.

When both keys are set, the service account is used. The quarterly backup copy to Drive writes files, so it needs the service account.

### Import

In **Expenses**, pick the month and click **Import month**. Each file is read with AI and waits for your check. Running it twice adds nothing twice. To import every morning, turn on **Daily sync** in **Settings > Expenses**.

### An index sheet, if you keep one

Optional. Some people keep a monthly spreadsheet of their expenses. When the month has one, the Ledger takes the rows from it instead of reading each file with AI.

- One Google Sheet per month, in the main folder, titled `Expense index YYYY-MM`, for example `Expense index 2026-10`. Change the title pattern in **Settings > Expenses**.
- **Download a sample sheet** in **Settings > Expenses** gives a CSV with every column and three sample rows. Open it in Google Sheets and choose **File > Save as Google Sheets**.
- The first row with a **Status** cell is the header row. Headers in English or Hebrew both work.

| Column | Required | What goes in it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Status | Yes | Expense to import the row. Not an expense, Personal document, Not obtained, Rejected not business or Rejected income to skip it. |
| Date | Yes | `2026-10-02` or `2/10/2026` |
| Supplier | Yes | The supplier's name |
| Total | Yes | Total including VAT, for example `118.00` |
| Currency | Yes | ILS, USD, EUR or GBP |
| VAT | No | The VAT part of the total |
| Supplier tax ID, Document type, Document number | No | As printed on the document |
| Category, Fixed, Notes | No | Your own labels. Fixed is Fixed or Not fixed. |
| File link | No | The Drive link to the receipt. The Ledger attaches that file to the expense. |

Rows with any other status, such as a totals row, are ignored.

## Not read automatically

Sometimes the AI reader can't read a file, most often because the AI provider is busy for a few minutes. The expense is saved anyway, with a **Not read** badge in the list and the reason on the expense.

- Open the expense and click **Read again**. Fields you already typed stay as they are.
- Or leave it. Every night the Ledger tries again, up to 4 reads in all, for 30 days.
- Or type the fields yourself. The file stays attached.

## Bank and card transactions

The Ledger collects receipts and invoices. With [Financy](https://financy.open-finance.ai/?ref=fin_01m5atfp5ctrp1b10fyq1pk71d) it also reads your bank and credit card transactions, read only, so it can find card charges with no receipt and deposits with no receipt.

### What you need

- A Financy plan with API access: Starter or higher. The free plan has no API.
- Your bank and card companies connected inside Financy. Financy adds them, the Ledger can't.

### Connect, once

1. In Financy: **Settings > API**. Copy the **Client ID**, **Client Secret** and **User ID**.
2. In the Ledger: **Settings > Expenses > Financy connection**. Paste the three values and click **Connect**. The Ledger tests them before it saves anything.
3. Tick the accounts and cards the business uses. Financy holds personal and business accounts together, and the Ledger reads only the ones you tick. Savings, loans and investments are never read.

### What you get

- **Dashboard > Financy Dashboard:** a tab built like Financy's own dashboard. See below.
- **Expenses > Bank activity:** each charge matched to an expense where one exists. An unmatched charge gets **Add as expense** (it waits for its receipt) or **Not a business expense**. A deposit that matches an open payment request gets **Record payment**, filled in for you to confirm.
- **Reports > Bank vs books:** money in and out from the bank next to what the Ledger recorded, with the gaps.
- **Claude:** the MCP tools `bank_activity`, `bank_balances` and `bank_summary`.

Every night the Ledger pulls the last 35 days. **Sync now** pulls on demand.

### The Financy Dashboard tab

Open **Dashboard** and click **Financy Dashboard**. It shows only the accounts you picked.

- **The top strip:** liquidity (cash in checking minus the current card charges, loans not counted), then income, expenses and net this month, each against last month.
- **Not counted:** a card bill paid from checking is the same money as the card charges, and a transfer between your own accounts is no money at all. The Ledger leaves both out of income and expenses and shows their sum under the strip.
- **Cash flow:** income and expenses for 3 or 6 months, with the numbers under the chart.
- **By category:** where the money went, or came from, by Financy's categories.
- **Accounts:** each checking account and card, with **Original** or **₪** for the balances.
- **Recent transactions:** each row has a status: Matched, To match, Suggested, Not business or Not counted.

A row marked Not counted by mistake: click **Count this**. It counts from then on, also after the next sync.

A charge the Ledger did not match: click **Match to expense** and pick the expense. A deposit: **Match to document** opens Record payment filled in, and you confirm there. **Unmatch** undoes a match.

### What the Ledger stores, and what it doesn't

It keeps the picked accounts' balances and transactions: date, amount, currency, description, merchant and Financy's category. It never stores your ID number, the account owner's name or a full account number. The Client Secret is encrypted and shows only its last 4 characters.

**Choose accounts** changes the picks. Unticking an account deletes its stored transactions. **Disconnect** stops the sync. **Delete bank data** removes everything pulled.

The Financy link is a partner link. If you join a paid plan, the Ledger's developer earns a commission.

Still stuck? [Write to us from the pricing page.](https://open-ledger.dev/en/pricing/#setup)

# From quote to receipt: your first documents

The order of documents in the Ledger, from a quote and a payment request to the receipt, and why the receipt is the one that counts.

Updated 2026-10-17

## The order

1. **Quote:** the price you offer. No tax meaning.
2. **Payment request** (דרישת תשלום): asks for the money. No tax meaning either.
3. **Receipt**, or for an עוסק מורשה a **tax invoice/receipt:** issued when the money arrives. This is the document that counts as income.

You skip steps you do not need. A client who already paid gets a receipt straight away.

## Make a payment request

1. Click **Create new**, then **Payment Request**.
2. Pick the client or add a new one. Add the lines: a service from **Services**, or free text, quantity and price.
3. Tick the payment methods to show.
4. Click **Save and finalize**. Finalizing gives it a number and locks it.
5. Send it: by email from the document page, or with the WhatsApp button, or download the PDF.

## When the money arrives

1. Open the payment request. In the list it has a **Record payment** button.
2. Fill in how and when the client paid, and the amount.
3. Confirm. The Ledger issues the receipt, numbered and signed, and links it to the request.
4. Send the receipt the same way.

## Mistakes

- **Before you send:Cancel** on the document page.
- **After you send:** a final document never changes. Open the receipt and click **Issue credit** for all or part of it.

## Recurring

For a monthly retainer, **Income > Recurring** issues a payment request or a receipt every month, and sends it if you choose **Issue and send automatically**.

Still stuck? [Write to us from the pricing page.](https://open-ledger.dev/en/pricing/#setup)

# First sign-in and setup

Sign in to your Ledger for the first time, fill in the business profile, logo, signature and numbering, and check one receipt before you go live.

Updated 2026-10-17

## Sign in

1. Open the Ledger's address from the installer's last screen or the Desktop summary.
2. Cloudflare shows its sign-in page. Type the owner email and click **Send me a code**.
3. Copy the code from the email and paste it. You are in.

Every sign-in works this way. A person whose email is not on the list never reaches the Ledger, Cloudflare stops them first.

## Business profile

The first sign-in opens the setup screen. The Ledger creates no document until the required fields hold a value: the business name in English and Hebrew, the tax number and the address. The same form lives in **Settings > Business**.

Optional fields print on documents when set: tagline, email, phone, website, and on payment requests also bank details and payment links.

## Logo and signature

- **Settings > Business > Logo > Upload image.** PNG, JPEG, WebP or SVG, up to 2 MB.
- **Settings > Signature > Signature image > Upload image.** A transparent PNG works best. It prints above the signer line on every issued document.

## Numbering, if you used another system before

**Settings > Numbering** lists one series per document type, each starting at 1. If you issued receipts or invoices in another system this year, set each series to one more than the last number you issued there.

Do this before the first document in that series. The start number locks the moment a document takes a number, and the Ledger refuses any later change.

## Payment methods

**Settings > Payment methods.** Add the ways clients pay you: bank transfer with your account details, Bit, card, a payment link. Payment requests list the ones you tick.

## Check before you go live

1. Issue one receipt to yourself for a small amount.
2. Open the client copy and the filed copy. Check the header, the tax number, the logo and the signature.
3. Check with your accountant: the document types you need, the business type, and sending documents digitally.

## Next

[From quote to receipt](https://open-ledger.dev/en/help/first-invoice/).

Still stuck? [Write to us from the pricing page.](https://open-ledger.dev/en/pricing/#setup)

# Install Open Ledger IL step by step

Every screen of the Windows installer, from the licence key to the Ledger's address, with what to fill in and what to skip.

Updated 2026-10-20

## The installer comes with your purchase

Buy the connected installer for ₪99, a first-release price (regular ₪199). The licence key and the download link reach your email within a minute.

- No Tax Authority API app to apply for. You connect through MTN's approved app.
- No Israeli server or relay to run. Every Tax Authority call leaves from an Israeli address, so it never gets the 403 a Worker abroad gets.
- No command line. A wizard creates the database, the files, the sign-in and the address in your Cloudflare account, in about 3 minutes.
- Run it again later to update, and your data stays.

[Buy the installer](https://get.open-ledger.dev/buy)[Or set it up yourself, free](https://github.com/matanlevanon/open-ledger-il/blob/main/docs/deploy.md)

The installer is the paid, connected way to install Open Ledger IL. You buy it once on the shop, and the purchase email brings the licence key and the download link. Read [Before you install](https://open-ledger.dev/en/help/before-you-start/) first.

## What the installer saves you

Setting up from the source code is free, and the [setup guide](https://github.com/matanlevanon/open-ledger-il/blob/main/docs/deploy.md) covers it. The installer skips the hard parts:

- **No Tax Authority API app.** On your own, you register in the Tax Authority developer portal, apply for an API app, wait for approval, and keep its client secret safe. The installer connects you through MTN's approved app. You sign in with your own Tax Authority user and that is all.
- **No Israeli server.** The Tax Authority turns away calls from outside Israel, and Cloudflare often serves a Worker from Frankfurt. On your own, you run a relay on a server with an Israeli address. With the installer, every call goes out through MTN's Israeli route.
- **No command line.** No Node.js, no wrangler, no database ids, no secrets to type. The wizard creates everything in your Cloudflare account in about 3 minutes.
- **Updates in one step.** Run the same installer again. It downloads the latest Ledger, and your data stays.

## 1. Download and open the installer

1. Click the download link in the purchase email. The file is `MTN-Open-Ledger-Setup.exe`, about 100 MB. Keep it. It downloads the latest Ledger while it runs, so the same file installs now and updates later.
2. The link works for 72 hours and 5 downloads. If it no longer works, open it anyway and click **Email me a fresh link**.
3. Double-click the file. Windows shows **Windows protected your PC**. Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. The file is not signed with a paid certificate yet, so Windows warns about every new copy.
4. The installer opens in your browser. Keep that browser tab and the small black window open until the end. Closing either one stops the install.

## 2. Licence key

Paste the licence key and the business tax number. The key works for this number only.

Click **Next**. The installer downloads the latest Ledger with your key and checks that it comes from MTN, unchanged. It shows the version when it is done, for example **Ledger 1.6.0 downloaded and checked.** If the download server does not answer and this computer ran the installer before, it offers **Use the saved Ledger** with its version and date.

## 3. Cloudflare account

The Ledger runs in your own Cloudflare account. The installer shows three steps, in order.

1. **No Cloudflare account yet?** Sign up at dash.cloudflare.com/sign-up with the business email and verify the email. Skip any offer to add a website.
2. **Turn on Zero Trust and R2.** Click **Show me how** on that step. Both are free, and both ask for a card. Do not create a bucket, the installer does that. Tick **I did it**.
3. **Create the API token.** Follow [Create the Cloudflare API token](https://open-ledger.dev/en/help/cloudflare-token/). This is the step where most people get stuck. Tick **I did it**.
4. Paste the token and click **Check token**. Pick the account.
5. Optional, on Windows: tick **Remember the token on this computer**. The next update fills it in. The token is stored encrypted for your Windows user, so anyone signed in as you on this PC could use it. Leave the box empty to paste the token each time.

## 4. Domain or workers.dev

After the token check, the installer asks for the Ledger's web address.

- **With a domain in Cloudflare:** type an address on it, for example `ledger.acme.co.il`. The installer creates it.
- **Without a domain:** tick **Use the free Cloudflare address instead of a domain** and choose a workers.dev name, for example the business name in English. Clients see this address in the links you send. Moving to your own domain later changes the address.

When the account already runs your Ledger, the address is filled in and locked, with the note "This account already runs your Ledger".

## 5. The business

1. Fill in the business name, the owner email and the business type: עוסק פטור, עוסק מורשה or חברה בע"מ. The Ledger asks once more on its first screen, so a mistake here is easy to fix.
2. Under **More people who may sign in**, add your accountant or a second email of your own, one per line. You also add people later, see [Give your accountant access](https://open-ledger.dev/en/help/users/).

On an update, the installer reads these details from your Ledger and shows them as a summary. Click **Edit details** to change one. The business type is locked: change it in the Ledger, under **Settings > Tax**.

## 6. Tax Authority

Pick how the Ledger gets allocation numbers for tax invoices. The connected edition fills this in for you: the Ledger connects through MTN, with nothing to type. After the install you sign in once with your Tax Authority user, see [Connect to the Tax Authority](https://open-ledger.dev/en/help/tax-authority/).

## 7. Extras

All optional. Each **?** button explains where to get the key.

- **Expense reading:** pick Gemini or Anthropic and paste the key. A Gemini key from aistudio.google.com starts with `AQ.`, older ones with `AIza`.
- **Email sending:** the Resend API key and the sender, written as `Business Name <billing@your-domain.co.il>`. See [Send documents by email](https://open-ledger.dev/en/help/email/).
- **Slack alerts:** the webhook address.

Skip anything you do not have. You add it later, see [Add or change a key after the install](https://open-ledger.dev/en/help/keys-later/). On an update, keys already set say **Already set. Leave empty to keep it.**

## 8. Install and finish

1. Check the summary and click **Install**. It shows the Ledger version. On an update the button reads **Update**, and the summary shows the move, for example **Updates your Ledger from 1.5.0 to 1.6.0**. It takes about 3 minutes.
2. The last screen shows the Ledger's address and an **MCP token**. Copy the token now, or click one of the download buttons. See [Connect Claude](https://open-ledger.dev/en/help/connect-claude/). Lost it later? **Settings > MCP** in the Ledger makes a new one.
3. It also shows your **email inbox** address, for forwarding receipts. See [Get your expenses into the Ledger](https://open-ledger.dev/en/help/expenses/).
4. The installer leaves a summary file on the Desktop, without secrets.
5. If you did not tick **Remember the token on this computer**, delete the Cloudflare API token: dash.cloudflare.com/profile/api-tokens, the three dots next to the token, **Delete**. The Ledger does not need it. If you ticked it, keep the token for the next update.

## Update later

Run the same installer again on the same Cloudflare account. It downloads the latest Ledger, finds your Ledger, fills in the address and the business details, keeps your data and keys, and the last button reads **Update**. On the same computer it also remembers your answers from the last run. See [Updates and backups](https://open-ledger.dev/en/help/updates-backups/).

## Next

[First sign-in and setup](https://open-ledger.dev/en/help/first-sign-in/).

Still stuck? [Write to us from the pricing page.](https://open-ledger.dev/en/pricing/#setup)

# Add or change a key after the install

Add the Gemini, Anthropic, Resend, Slack or Google Drive key to your Ledger in the Cloudflare dashboard, without running the installer again.

Updated 2026-10-17

The Ledger reads its keys from its Worker in Cloudflare. A Worker is the program that runs the Ledger. You add or change a key there.

## Where

1. Sign in at dash.cloudflare.com.
2. In the left menu, under **Build**, open **Compute > Workers & Pages** and click **mtn-open-ledger**.
3. Open the **Settings** tab. The first section is **Runtime variables and secrets**.
4. Click **Add variable**. Type the name under **Key** and paste the value under **Value**. For a key, tick **Secret**. For a plain setting, leave it clear.
5. Click **Add variable and deploy**. The Ledger uses the new value within a minute.

To change a value that is already there, click the pencil on its row, paste the new value and deploy.

Cloudflare then shows a banner: "Update your Wrangler configuration with these changes to keep deployments in sync." It is meant for people who deploy from source code. Close it with the X. The installer keeps your values when you update.

Names are exact, in capital letters.

## Which names

- **Receipt reading with Gemini:** Secret `GEMINI_API_KEY` with the key, and the plain variable `AI_PROVIDER` with the value `gemini`.
- **Receipt reading with Anthropic:** Secret `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` with the key, and the plain variable `AI_PROVIDER` with the value `anthropic`. If the note on an expense says the key is not tied to a workspace, add the plain variable `ANTHROPIC_WORKSPACE_ID` with the workspace id (`wrkspc_...`) from console.anthropic.com.
- **A different reading model:** the plain variable `GEMINI_MODEL` or `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` with the model name. Use it when reading is slow or a model is retired.
- **Email sending:** Secret `MAIL_API_KEY` with the Resend key, and the plain variable `MAIL_FROM` with the sender, for example `Acme Ltd <billing@acme.co.il>`.
- **Slack alerts:** Secret `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL`.
- **Google Drive expenses:** Secret `GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON` with the whole content of the JSON key file, from the first `{` to the last `}`. For a folder shared by link, the secret `GOOGLE_API_KEY` with a Google API key instead.
- **MCP token:** Secret `MCP_TOKEN`, see [Connect Claude](https://open-ledger.dev/en/help/connect-claude/).

## Rules

- Never paste a key in an email, a chat or a document. Paste it only into Cloudflare or the installer.
- If a key leaks, make a new one at the provider, delete the old one there, and replace it here.

Still stuck? [Write to us from the pricing page.](https://open-ledger.dev/en/pricing/#setup)

# Take payments with Grow, Cardcom or another provider

Use a card payment provider for collecting money and the Ledger for the receipts, by hand or automatically, without two documents for one payment.

Updated 2026-10-17

The Ledger issues the documents. A payment provider such as Grow, Cardcom, PayPlus or Bit collects the money. The two work side by side.

## First: turn off the provider's documents

Most providers issue their own receipt or invoice for every payment. Turn that off in the provider's settings, or ask their support to. Otherwise every payment gets two documents with two different numbers, and your books stop matching the bank.

## Way 1: by hand

1. In the Ledger, add the provider's payment link as a payment method: **Settings > Payment methods**, type **Card** or **Other**, paste the link.
2. Send the client a payment request with that method ticked.
3. When the provider tells you the money arrived, open the payment request and click **Record payment**. Pick **Card**, and paste the provider's transaction number as the reference.
4. The Ledger issues the receipt. Send it to the client.

Two minutes per payment. Fits a business with a few payments a week.

## Way 2: automatic, for technical users

The Ledger has an MCP endpoint, a door for other software, at its address followed by `/mcp`. It takes JSON-RPC calls (`tools/call`) with the header `Authorization: Bearer` and your MCP token. The tools include `list_clients`, `create_draft`, `finalize_document`, `record_payment` and `add_expense`.

An automation tool such as Make, Zapier or n8n connects the provider to it:

1. In the provider, turn on the webhook for successful payments and point it at a new scenario.
2. In the scenario, find the client with `list_clients`, using the payer's name or email.
3. Record the payment against the open payment request with `record_payment` and `confirm: true`. The scenario needs the payment request's document id. Keep a small table of payment link to document id, filled when you send each request.
4. The Ledger issues the receipt.

This takes an afternoon to set up and test. Start with one small payment. For the MCP token, see [Connect Claude or another app](https://open-ledger.dev/en/help/connect-claude/).

Still stuck? [Write to us from the pricing page.](https://open-ledger.dev/en/pricing/#setup)

# Connect to the Tax Authority for allocation numbers

Allocation numbers with the installer or with your own setup: what each path takes, how to connect, and the 90-day reconnect.

Updated 2026-10-17

A tax invoice to an Israeli עוסק מורשה above the threshold needs an allocation number (מספר הקצאה) from the Tax Authority. With a connection, the Ledger asks for the number when you finalize the invoice and prints it on the document.

An עוסק פטור issues no tax invoices, so it needs no connection. Connect later, when you become עוסק מורשה.

## Two ways to connect

| | With the installer | Self setup from the source code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tax Authority API app | MTN's approved app. Nothing to apply for | Register in the developer portal, apply for your own app, wait for approval |
| Client id and secret | None. The installer sets the connection | You store them as Worker secrets |
| Calls from Israel | Always, through MTN's Israeli route | The Tax Authority turns away calls from outside Israel. You catch Cloudflare's Tel Aviv data center some of the time, or run your own relay on an Israeli server |
| Setup time | Part of the 3-minute install | Hours, plus the approval wait |
| Cost | Included in the installer price | Free, plus any server you run |

## With the installer

1. In the Ledger, open **ITA** in the sidebar.
2. Click **Connect to ITA**.
3. The Tax Authority's sign-in page opens. Sign in with the business's own Tax Authority user: the user code and the one-time code sent to your phone.
4. Approve the request. The consent screen names MTN's app. You come back to the Ledger, and the page shows **Connected**, with the days left.

## Self setup

1. Register in the Tax Authority developer portal and create an API app for Israel Invoices. Wait for production approval.
2. Put the app's client id and secret in the Worker's secrets, as the [setup guide](https://github.com/matanlevanon/open-ledger-il/blob/main/docs/deploy.md) lists.
3. Solve the Israel-only rule. On the ITA page, click **Check route**. "Direct (from TLV): reached the ITA" means the call got through this time. "From FRA: turned away, HTTP 403" means Cloudflare served you from Frankfurt. For calls that work every time, run the relay from `tools/ita-relay` on a server with an Israeli address, for example Oracle Cloud's free tier in Jerusalem.
4. Then **Connect to ITA** as above.

No app at all? The Ledger also runs in manual mode: each invoice that needs a number waits on the ITA page, you request the number in the Tax Authority web app, and type it back.

[Buy the installer](https://open-ledger.dev/en/help/install/) to skip steps 1 to 3.

## Every 90 days

The Tax Authority login lasts 90 days on both paths. The ITA page shows **Login ends in N days**. With Slack alerts on, the Ledger warns you on days 75, 85 and 89. When it ends, open **ITA** and click **Connect again**. An invoice still waiting for a number shows in the **Allocation queue** on the same page. After you reconnect, click **Retry now**.

## When a number is refused

The ITA page shows the reason. The choices are to cancel the invoice, continue without a number with a notice on the document, or switch to reverse charge with the client's agreement. Ask your accountant which fits.

Still stuck? [Write to us from the pricing page.](https://open-ledger.dev/en/pricing/#setup)

# Common problems and how to fix them

Fixes for the places people get stuck: Windows warnings, the Cloudflare token, Zero Trust, keys the installer refuses, sign-in, downloads and email.

Updated 2026-10-17

## The installer

- **Windows protected your PC.** Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**.
- **The antivirus removed the file.** Restore it from the antivirus quarantine and allow it, or download it again from the purchase email.
- **Nothing opens after double-click.** Wait 20 seconds, the file is large. The installer opens a browser tab at an address starting with `http://127.0.0.1`. If no tab opens, copy that address from the small black window into your browser.
- **The licence key is refused.** Type it as `OL-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX`, and check the tax number. The key works only for the tax number it was bought for. Reinstalling the same business with the same key is fine.

## Cloudflare

- **Zone Resources is missing.** It shows up only after a Zone permission row. Without a domain, skip it and use the free workers.dev address. See [Create the Cloudflare API token](https://open-ledger.dev/en/help/cloudflare-token/).
- **Check token fails.** The message names the missing permission. Edit the token, add the row, save, and check again.
- **Zero Trust or R2 asks for a card.** Both free plans ask for a payment method and charge nothing.
- **Purchase R2 Plan.** In the left menu, **Storage & databases > R2 Object Storage**. Click it and confirm the free tier. The first 10 GB a month are free.

## Keys

- **A Gemini key is refused.** New keys from Google AI Studio start with `AQ.`. The installer from version 1.6.0 of 17 October 2026 accepts them. With an older installer, pick **No** for expense reading and add the key afterwards, see [Add or change a key](https://open-ledger.dev/en/help/keys-later/).
- **An Anthropic key is refused.** It starts with `sk-ant-`. Copy it again from console.anthropic.com.

## Signing in

- **A Cloudflare page asks for an email.** That is the sign-in. Type the owner email and paste the code from the email.
- **No code arrives.** Check spam, and check that the email is the one given in the installer.
- **Someone else is stopped at the Cloudflare page.** Add their email in Cloudflare Access, see [Give your accountant access](https://open-ledger.dev/en/help/users/).

## Downloads and email

- **The download link says it expired or ran out.** Click **Email me a fresh link** on that page.
- **Clients get your documents in spam.** See [Keep them out of spam](https://open-ledger.dev/en/help/email/).
- **Lost the MCP token.** See [Connect Claude](https://open-ledger.dev/en/help/connect-claude/).

## Tax Authority

- **ITA says reconnect.** The login lasts 90 days. Open **ITA** and click **Connect again**.
- **An invoice waits for a number for 24 hours.** Request the number in the Tax Authority web app and type it on the ITA page.

Still stuck? [Write to us from the pricing page.](https://open-ledger.dev/en/pricing/#setup)

# Updates and backups

How to check for a new Open Ledger IL version and update with the installer, and where the Ledger keeps its backups.

Updated 2026-10-20

## Check for updates

**Settings > Updates > Check for updates.** The Ledger also checks on the 1st of each month. Nothing installs by itself.

## Update

1. Run the same installer again: `MTN-Open-Ledger-Setup.exe`, the file you kept. It downloads the latest Ledger while it runs. Lost the file? Open the download link from your purchase email. If it no longer works, open it anyway and click **Email me a fresh link**.
2. Run it on the same Cloudflare account, with the same licence key.
3. It updates the Ledger and keeps everything: the database, the files, the sign-in and your keys.

After you paste the Cloudflare token, the installer finds the Ledger in your account and fills in the business details from it. The web address and the business type are locked on an update. Keys already set stay as they are when you leave their fields empty. The summary before **Update** shows the move, for example **Updates your Ledger from 1.5.0 to 1.6.0**. If the installer says it is too old for the current Ledger, download the new installer from your purchase email. On the same computer, the installer also remembers your answers from the last run, and the token too if you tick **Remember the token on this computer** (Windows only, stored encrypted for your Windows user).

## Backups

- Every quarter, the Ledger writes a full copy of its database and a list of every file to its own backup bucket, and tests that the copy restores.
- With Google Drive connected, the same copy also goes to your Drive, outside Cloudflare.
- Every night it checks the numbering for gaps and the documents for changes. **Settings > Backups > Run check now** runs the check on demand.

## Keep Cloudflare safe

The Cloudflare account holds your books. Turn on two-factor sign-in: dash.cloudflare.com, the person icon on the top right, **Profile**, then **Access Management > Authentication**, **Two-Factor Authentication**.

Still stuck? [Write to us from the pricing page.](https://open-ledger.dev/en/pricing/#setup)

# Give your accountant or assistant access

Add an accountant, an assistant or your second email to the Ledger, in the Ledger and in Cloudflare Access, and remove them again.

Updated 2026-10-17

Each person gets a role per business.

- **Owner:** everything, including Settings, users, numbering and the Tax Authority connection.
- **Assistant:** clients, quotes, payment requests, receipts, sending and expenses. No Settings, users or Tax Authority.
- **Accountant:** reads what you allow, until an end date. Every request is logged. An accountant never issues or cancels a document.

## Add a person

Two places, both needed.

### 1. In the Ledger

1. Pick the business in the switcher at the top.
2. In the sidebar, open **Accountant > Users**.
3. Click **Invite someone**.
4. Type the email and pick the role. An accountant also needs an end date and the feature switches: income documents, expenses, reports, the monthly pack, the unified file.
5. Click **Send invite**.

For your own second email, pick **Owner**.

### 2. In Cloudflare Access

Emails you listed in the installer are there already. For anyone new:

1. Sign in at dash.cloudflare.com. In the left menu, under **Protect & connect**, open **Zero Trust**.
2. Go to **Access controls > Applications** and find **MTN Open Ledger** in the list.
3. In its row, click the policy name in the **Policies** column. The policy opens for editing.
4. Under **Include > Emails**, add the email.
5. Click **Save policy**.

Until step 5, Cloudflare stops the person at its own sign-in page.

## Remove a person

A business always keeps one owner. The only owner has no Remove button and its role is locked. Add another owner first.

1. In the Ledger: **Accountant > Users**, click **Revoke** on the row.
2. In Cloudflare Access: open the same policy, remove the email from **Include > Emails** and click **Save policy**.

Still stuck? [Write to us from the pricing page.](https://open-ledger.dev/en/pricing/#setup)
